descriptionChirho: To divide, share, or apportion something among recipients in the basic Qal active stem; the fundamental sense of splitting or distributing property, land, spoil, or portions, confirmed by Arabic قَسَمَ (qasama), Korean 나누다 (nanuda), and Swahili -gawanya.

To distribute or divide up thoroughly in the intensive Piel stem, emphasizing the completeness or deliberateness of the distribution; Arabic Form II يُقَسِّمُ (yuqassimu) vs Qal Form I يَقْسِمُ (yaqsimu) confirms the intensified binyan distinction, while Korean 나누다 and Swahili -gawanya remain the same as Qal.

To scatter or disperse people, a metaphorical extension of the Piel 'divide' sense where the result is diaspora rather than orderly distribution; confirmed by Korean 흩어졌네 (scattered) and Swahili -tawanya (scatter), distinct from -gawanya (distribute).

To cause someone to receive a portion or to allot a share in the Hifil causative stem; Korean 분배하려고 (bunbaeharyeogo, 'in order to apportion') and Swahili kupokea sehemu ('to receive a portion') highlight the causative-benefactive nuance.

To be divided or split passively in the Nifal stem, where the subject undergoes division rather than performing it; Arabic انْقَسَمَ (inqasama, Form VII passive) and Korean 나누어지다 (nanueoejida, passive of divide) confirm the passive valence.

To be distributed or divided up as the passive of the Piel intensive stem, indicating that thorough distribution has been carried out upon the subject; Arabic تُقَسَّمُ (tuqassamu, Form II passive) and Swahili -gawanywa (passive) confirm the passive-intensive reading.

To divide something among themselves in the Hitpael reflexive-reciprocal stem, where multiple parties mutually share or partition; Arabic يَقْتَسِمُوها (yaqtasimuhaa, Form VIII reciprocal) and Swahili -gawana (reciprocal of -gawa) confirm the reciprocal valence.
